floor_history.headline: recon: honest floor 48 -> 47 (xor operand order); residual attributed to sched1 block-5 multiply order (~38), un-coalesced dist copy into $a0 (~5, sibling func_8002D518's closed residual), and reorg s

frontier.hypothesis: Block-5 multiply order (cluster 1, ~38 insns) is reachable by a natural expression shape: cx/cz computed inline at their use points (explains the deferred cz sra/subu) or a per-edge helper-macro evaluation order.
frontier.mechanism: sched1 backward list scheduling with LUID tie-break (tools/gcc-2.7.2/sched.c rank_for_schedule)
frontier.next_probe: tools/sched_solver inverse on block 5 against the target order to get the required emission order/dependency shape, then spell and sweep; BB2_RANK_DEBUG=1 on tools/gcc-2.7.2/cc1 via tmp/grind/func_8002D780/s1/dbrdbg.py to see class ties

frontier.hypothesis: The `dist` copy into $a0 (cluster 2) needs a second pseudo that survives cse: compute the sqrt input as its own expression separate from the call argument, or a u32-typed macro-style block.
frontier.mechanism: global.c conflict: dist stays live across the calls in $s1; a copy that dies before the calls lands in $a0
frontier.next_probe: sweep natural forms first; only if spent, the sibling func_8002D518 FAKE dead-store re-store family with this function's own exhaustion ledger; also check the LZCR slot offset (target 16($sp), ours 0($sp))

frontier.hypothesis: The tail fill (cluster 3, 3 insns) follows once the call-3 block entry has $v0 dead in reorg's liveness walk, e.g. by giving that block a label or by avoiding jump1's relocation of the shared return-1 block.
frontier.mechanism: reorg.c mark_target_live_regs pending-dead flush at CODE_LABELs (tools/gcc-2.7.2/reorg.c:2560-2760)
frontier.next_probe: sweep tail shapes and read the BB2_DBR_DEBUG `insn=381` line for oppregs bit 2 (tmp/grind/func_8002D780/s1/dbrdbg.py BB2_DBR_DEBUG)
